# Wilmington University Corner

> A law school study library: outlines, rule charts, flowcharts, flashcards, and practice question banks you can open in the browser or download.

Machine-readable endpoints (static JSON, CORS-friendly via GitHub Pages):
- [Catalog](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/catalog.json): every subject and document with metadata and URLs
- [Search index](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/search-index.json): compact index for keyword search
- [OpenAPI spec](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/openapi.json): describes the endpoints above
- [Full text](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/llms-full.txt): plain text of every document in one file

Authoring specs, for agents that write new outlines, supplements, practice sets and flashcard decks in the formats the site builds and links automatically:
- [Spec index](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/index.json): every spec and template below, with media types
- [Outline format (outline/v1)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/outline-format.md): How to write a Word outline the site turns into headings, callouts and case cards, and that the reference popup indexes (sections, case keys, worked problems).
- [Statutory / rule supplement format (supplement/v1)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/supplement-format.md): The AREAS and DATA contract behind a course supplement and the reference popup, and the citation styles (ucc, fre, mrpc, frcp, restatement, section).
- [MCQ practice set format (mcq/v1)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/mcq-format.md): The canonical multiple-choice schema, the Shuffle-mode practice page it builds into, and the citation rules that make every question link to the supplement and outline.
- [Flashcard deck format (cards/v1)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/cards-format.md): The canonical flashcard schema and the study page it builds into: one card at a time, shuffle, remove, and an all-cards overview.
- [Prompt templates](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/ai-prompts.md): Copy-paste prompts for generating an outline, a supplement, a practice set and a flashcard deck in these formats.
- [MCQ practice page template](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/mcq-shuffle-template.html): The standalone Shuffle-mode practice page with a sample mcq/v1 set; replace the JSON in its mcq-data block.
- [Supplement viewer template](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/supplement-template.html): The standalone supplement viewer with sample UCC data; replace its SUPP, AREAS and DATA lines.
- [Flashcard page template](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/cards-template.html): The standalone flashcard page with a sample cards/v1 deck; replace the JSON in its cards-data block.
- [Sample mcq/v1 set](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/sample.mcq.json): Six Sales and Leases questions using every mcq/v1 feature.
- [Sample supplement/v1 data](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/sample.supplement.json): Seven UCC sections in the supplement/v1 format.
- [Sample cards/v1 deck](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/sample.cards.json): Eight Evidence flashcards using every cards/v1 field.
- [Sample outline/v1 data](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/sample-outline.json): An outline as data, for scripts/templates/build-outline-docx.mjs.
- [Sample outline (Word)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/specs/sample-outline.docx): sample-outline.json built into the Word file the site reads.

## Evidence

Federal Rules of Evidence, Weeks 1–15 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion, expert reliability, authentication and the best evidence rule, and privileges. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

- [Evidence Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–1098). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Part IX covers expert bases and reliability (703, 705, Frye, Daubert, Joiner, Kumho Tire). Part X covers authentication and the best evidence rule (901–902, 1001–1008). Part XI covers Rule 501, the psychotherapist and lawyer-client privileges, 502 waiver, government lawyers, and self-incrimination. Part XII covers the spousal and marital-confidences privileges. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.
- [Evidence Rules Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rules-outline.txt): Outline. The condensed outline with the case cards taken out, for reviewing by rule. It covers the same twelve parts and 35 sections, Weeks 1–15, and keeps every rule box, black-letter rule, exam tip, and step-by-step checklist. Holdings the course tests are restated as rules in the sections they govern, such as the Peña-Rodriguez exception to 606(b), the Gordon factors, the Daubert factors, the Jaffee psychotherapist privilege, Swidler & Berlin, Zolin's crime-fraud procedure, and Trammel's spousal privilege.
- [Evidence Rule Chart/outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rule-chart.txt): Rule Chart. The master rule chart for Weeks 1–5. Each rule is explained in plain English with a note on what to watch out for. Rows tagged by class come from the Class 1–10 lecture slides, and there are notes on what the midterm covers.
- [Federal Rules of Evidence](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/federal-rules-of-evidence.txt): Document. The full official text of all 69 Federal Rules of Evidence, as amended to December 1, 2024, with notes on the 2023 and 2024 amendments and the Rule 801(d)(1)(A) amendment taking effect December 1, 2026. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 803(2) to go straight to the excited-utterance exception, or 404(b)(2) to see that clause marked), filter to the rules the course covers or to any of eleven course topics, and follow cross-references between rules. Each rule shows how often the outline and the practice sets cite it. The practice sets use it for their Look up popup: any rule cited in a question or explanation opens its text with the cited subdivision marked.
- [Evidence Flowcharts](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rule-flowcharts.txt): Flowcharts. Interactive decision charts for Weeks 1–5. Zoom and pan around each chart, walk through a rule one step at a time, and search all nine charts. Covers relevance (401–403), the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), impeachment, 609 convictions, the 412 rape shield, and 606(b) jury secrecy.
- [Evidence Rules Flashcards](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rules-flashcards.txt): Flashcards. 236 flashcards for every rule, test and tested holding in the Evidence Rules Outline, Weeks 1–15, in outline order: jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy rules, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, lay and expert opinion, authentication and best evidence, and privileges. Each card asks for one rule or test; elements and factors are listed the way the outline labels them, with the outline
- [FRE Rule Cards](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/fre-rule-cards.txt): Flashcards. Flashcards for the Federal Rules of Evidence in Weeks 1–5. Pick your topics, flip each card, and rate yourself with a tap or a swipe. Missed cards come back sooner, and your mastery is saved in your browser.
- [Evidence Comprehensive Practice Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-comprehensive-practice-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 150 bar-style questions on all of Weeks 1–15, in five sets of 30, each covering every topic. It keeps the 100 hardest questions from the earlier Weeks 1–5 and hearsay sets, now with five choices each, and adds 50 new questions on the material they never reached: competency, Chambers and Bruton, lay and expert opinion through Daubert, Joiner, and Kumho Tire, authentication and the best evidence rule, and the lawyer-client, psychotherapist, and spousal privileges. It covers jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), and 413–415, impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, and the Confrontation Clause, and applies the 2023–2026 amendments, including the December 1, 2026 change to Rule 801(d)(1)(A). Five choices each, and every choice is explained.
- [Evidence Concepts Test](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-concepts-test.txt): Practice Questions. A 116-question concepts test on the whole course, Weeks 1–15, in outline order: jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), and 413–415, impeachment and the rape shield, the hearsay definition, 801(d), and the 803–807 exceptions, the Confrontation Clause through Smith v. Arizona, completeness, Bruton, and the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion through Daubert and Kumho Tire, authentication and the best evidence rule, and the lawyer-client, psychotherapist, and spousal privileges. Each question turns on a holding, an element, or a recent amendment, and its wrong choices are the dissents, overruled cases, and older rules students mix up. Five choices each. Tutor mode grades as you go; timed mode gives you 90 seconds a question. Every question has the rule, an analysis, and why each choice is right or wrong.
- [Evidence Most Testable Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-most-testable-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 60 five-choice questions on the most testable material from Weeks 1–15, in two sets of 30. About a third is hearsay, followed by character evidence, impeachment, confrontation, expert testimony, and privileges. Every question uses new facts, and every choice is explained.
- [Evidence Most Testable Questions II](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-most-testable-questions-ii.txt): Practice Questions. 60 more five-choice questions on the most testable material from Weeks 1–15, in two sets of 30, testing different rule points from the first collection. About a third is hearsay, and it adds jury secrecy, competency, Rule 411, Rule 106, and compulsory process. Every question uses new facts, and every choice is explained.
- [Evidence Bar Exam Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-bar-exam-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 99 hard bar-style questions on all of Weeks 1–15, in three sets of 33. Each set covers every topic, and together they test every section of the outline: jury secrecy and competency, relevance and 403, the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), and 413–415, impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, and the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion, authentication and the best evidence rule, and privileges. Each question gives a longer fact pattern that sets two rules against each other, and the wrong choices give the right result for the wrong reason, use the neighboring rule, or apply an old version of an amended rule. The set includes the 2023–2026 amendments. Five choices each, and every choice is explained.
- [Evidence Best Answer Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-best-answer-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 69 tricky bar-style questions on all of Weeks 1–15, in two sets (34 and 35), each covering every topic. Each question has two or three defensible choices, and you have to pick the best one, the way the bar exam does. Often that is the answer you

## Professional Responsibility

Model Rules of Professional Conduct, Weeks 1–15 (Burk, Ethical Lawyering, Chs. 1–25): regulating lawyers and bar admission, forming and ending the client-lawyer relationship, competence, confidentiality, agency and fiduciary duty, fees and client funds, conflicts of interest, government lawyers and prosecutors, ethics in advocacy, law firms and organizational clients, public service, duties to third parties, advertising and solicitation, and harassment and discrimination.

- [Professional Responsibility Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/pr-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Burk, Ethical Lawyering, Chs. 1–25, and the Model Rules with their Comments), in syllabus order. Part I covers regulating lawyers: sources of law, bar admission and discipline, unauthorized practice, the consequences of misconduct, and why smart people do stupid things. Part II covers the MR 1.0 definitions, competence and diligence, the duty of care and ineffective assistance, forming the relationship, scope, duties to non-clients, clients with decision-making limitations (MR 1.14), and declining and withdrawing. Part III covers confidentiality, privilege and work product, and the MR 1.6(b) exceptions. Part IV covers the lawyer as fiduciary and agent, candor under MR 1.4, and the allocation of authority. Part V covers fees, retainers, fee sharing, and trust accounts. Part VI covers conflicts: personal-interest conflicts under MR 1.8, concurrent and former clients, imputation and screening, and consent. Part VII covers government lawyers, the revolving door (MR 1.11, 1.12), and prosecutors (MR 3.8). Part VIII covers ethics in advocacy (MR 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.9). Part IX covers supervision in law firms, selling a practice, and organizational clients (MR 1.13). Part X covers public service (MR 6.1–6.5). Part XI covers truthfulness, represented and unrepresented persons, client wrongdoing, threats and reporting, restrictions on practice, and advertising and solicitation. Part XII covers MR 8.4(g), and Part XIII has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, the class quiz answers for Chs. 22, 24, and 25 worked in, and case cards for the cases the readings rely on, including the assigned Bradwell and Zauderer.
- [ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/aba-model-rules.txt): Document. The full text of all 56 ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct with all 449 Comments. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 1.7(a)(2) to see that clause marked, or MR 1.18 to go straight there), filter to the rules the course covers or to any of the outline's twelve parts, follow cross-references between rules, and open or close all the Comments at once. Each rule shows how often the outline and the practice sets cite it, and the Comments they rely on are marked. The practice sets use it for their Look up popup: any rule cited in a question or explanation opens its text with the cited paragraph or Comment marked.
- [Pro Rep Drill](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/mpre-drill-v3.txt): Practice Questions. 355 original MPRE-style application questions on Chs. 1–9, 20, 21 and the class slides. Use study mode for instant feedback or exam mode to be graded at the end. Filter by topic and shuffle the answer order.
- [MPRE 500 Practice Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/mpre-500-practice-questions.txt): Practice Questions. All 500 questions in Stevenson, 500 MPRE Practice Questions (2019), in the book
- [Course Quiz](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/pr-course-quiz.txt): Practice Questions. The 54 multiple-choice questions from the class quizzes on Chs. 5, 6, 8, 20, and 21, checked against the course answer keys. Take the quiz for a score or open the answer view, with explanations drawn from Ethical Lawyering, the class slides, and the Model Rules.

## Con Law II

Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13). Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, immoral speech, torts involving speech, commercial speech, content-neutral rules and expressive conduct, government speech, funding and forum doctrine, government employees and public schools, and social media and elections.

- [First Amendment Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-outline.txt): Outline. Case-by-case outline of Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13), from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, New York Times v. Sullivan, Central Hudson, Texas v. Johnson, Shurtleff, Rosenberger, Tinker, NetChoice, and Citizens United. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes checklists for each doctrine, synthesis tables, and the stretch exercises. Every case box opens in the Look up panel on the practice pages.
- [First Amendment Outline (PDF)](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-outline-pdf.txt): Outline. The same Weeks 1–15 outline (Chapters 1–13) as a 74-page PDF to download or print.
- [First Amendment Concepts Test](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-concepts-test.txt): Practice Questions. 110 concept questions on the whole course, Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13), in outline order: the Religion Clauses, the speech framework and unprotected categories, immoral speech, defamation and IIED, commercial speech, time, place, and manner rules and expressive conduct, government speech, funding and forum doctrine, employee and student speech, and social media and elections. It works like Shuffle mode: shuffled choices, cross-outs, an explanation for every choice, the rule, Retry missed, and a link to the outline section to review. Filter by chapter or shuffle the whole set.
- [First Amendment Bar Exam Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-bar-exam-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 120 bar-style questions on all of Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13), in four practice finals of 30, each sized like the final

## Sales and Leases

Sales and Leases of Goods under UCC Articles 1, 2 and 2A, Weeks 1–14 (Sepinuck, Chapters 1–7, 9 and 11). Covers which law governs, formation and the battle of the forms, the statute of frauds, warranties and disclaimers, gap fillers, delivery and risk of loss, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, repudiation, excuse, buyer's and seller's remedies, rejection, cure and revocation, privity, and leases under Article 2A.

- [Sales and Leases Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed outline of Weeks 1–14 for the final exam. 35 sections. Sections I–XVI cover Weeks 1–8: the UCC and governing law, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds and unconscionability, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, quantity and price, delivery and risk of loss, disclaimers, remedy limits, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse. Sections XVII–XXXV follow the syllabus through Week 14: buyer's remedies, rejection, cure, acceptance and revocation, privity, seller's remedies, Article 2A leases and finance leases, and final-exam checklists, with every assigned problem worked. Case boxes mark main, note, and cited-only cases with their casebook pages and class slides. Slides on file end at Week 8, so later sections rest on the casebook and statutes.
- [Sales and Leases Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 444 bar-style multiple-choice questions on Weeks 1–14: the rules, cases, and assigned problems in the outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, buyer's and seller's remedies, privity, and leases under Article 2A. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.
- [Sales and Leases Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 58 cumulative practice exams (870 questions) for the final, covering all of Weeks 1–14 and all 35 sections of the course outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, buyer's and seller's remedies, privity, and leases under Article 2A. Each exam follows Professor Richardson's sample-exam format: 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions that mix rule questions (“Which of the following is NOT…”) with short hypos asking who wins and why, plus “None of the above” and “All of the above” choices that are sometimes the answer. Every exam samples the whole course, and about 40% of the questions come from the Weeks 8–14 remedies and lease units, including integrated hypos and damages calculations. Every choice has its own explanation. Use Study mode to check answers as you go, or Exam mode to grade a full exam, and pick a topic to drill one outline section by week.
- [Sales and Leases Statutory Supplement](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-statutory-supplement.txt): Document. Every UCC section the Weeks 1-14 outline and the practice sets cite (182 sections from Articles 1, 2, 2A, and 9), from Selected Commercial Statutes, 2026 edition, with the Official Comments. Section text is summarized in the statute's own key words and each comment is condensed; comments the outline or the practice questions rely on are marked. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 2-207 to go straight there), filter by any of the outline's first 34 sections, follow cross-references between sections, and open or close all the comments at once.

## Agency & Partnership

Business Associations, Weeks 1–8 (Bainbridge, Park & Rodrigues, 6th ed.). Covers creating an agency, actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, a principal's tort liability, agents' fiduciary duties, choosing an entity, partnership formation under the UPA and RUPA, partners' rights, authority and duties, dissociation and dissolution, loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs.

- [Agency & Partnership Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–8, built from the Class 1–8 slides, the casebook, and the 2026 statutory supplement. Part I covers agency: creating the relationship, contract liability and authority, tort liability, and fiduciary duties. Part II covers business entities: choosing an entity, partnership formation, economic rights and property, management and authority, partners' fiduciary duties, dissociation and dissolution, Kovacik loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every case (62 main cases plus slide references and supplemental readings).
- [Agency & Partnership Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 284 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and slide problem in the Weeks 1–8 outline, across 23 topics: creating an agency, actual, apparent and inherent authority, ratification, estoppel, agents' contract and tort liability, scope of employment, independent contractors, and agents' fiduciary duties; then entity selection, partnership formation, property, management and authority, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, loss sharing, buyouts, limited partnerships, LLPs, and LLCs. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 14 practice exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, written in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam: 15 five-choice questions each, with six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from creating an agency through authority, ratification, estoppel, tort liability, and agents' duties, to partnership formation, property, management, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, Kovacik loss sharing, buyouts, LPs, LLPs, and LLCs. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams II](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams-ii.txt): Practice Questions. A second set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the same format as the first: Professor Richardson's sample-exam style, with 15 five-choice questions per exam, six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." All 28 hypos are new fact patterns, among them a term partnership that loses a partner, an art collector's undisclosed agent, a plumber's detour and frolic, a grocery run by three partners, a hospital buyer's self-dealing, a UPA print shop's liquidation, a manager-managed LLC, a joint venture's taken opportunity, an LLP before and after its filing, and a dentists' buyout agreement. Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams III](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams-iii.txt): Practice Questions. A third set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the same format as the first two: Professor Richardson's sample-exam style, with 15 five-choice questions per exam, six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." All 28 hypos are new fact patterns, among them a vineyard partner's expulsion, a nephew selling his aunt's car, a solar lender that runs its borrower, a nightclub bouncer, a UPA laundromat freeze-out, a fired club manager's lingering authority, a coffee franchisor's espresso machines, an LLC formed after its lease was signed, a town's fireworks contractor, a festival lot's taken lease, a surf shop's winding up, and a lender to a cidery. Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Concept Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-concept-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 14 concept exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam (15 five-choice questions each, with combination choices such as "B and C" and "None of the above"), but built around the rules rather than long fact patterns. The questions test the fine distinctions: the UPA (1914) against the RUPA on entity versus aggregate theory, property, liability, dissolution, and buyouts; general partnerships against LLPs, LPs, LLLPs, and LLCs on filing, control, liability, agency, and exit; the Restatement (Second) against the Restatement (Third); and which defaults a partnership or operating agreement can and cannot change. Questions 1–6 stand alone, and Questions 7–11 and 12–15 share a focus note naming the topic and statute, such as UPA dissolution, RUPA Article 7 buyouts, LLP shields, or managing an LLC. Every choice has its own explanation, and the exams cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

## Contracts I

Contracts I, Weeks 1–9 (Epstein, Markell & Ponoroff, Making and Doing Deals, 7th ed.). Covers whether there is an enforceable agreement, the objective theory of assent, offers and their termination, options and firm offers, methods of acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and UCC § 2-207, misunderstanding, indefiniteness and letters of intent, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation.

- [Contracts I Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/contracts-i/contracts-i-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–9 on the Fall 2026 syllabus. Part I covers formation: enforceable agreements and which law governs, objective assent and implied-in-fact contracts, offers, termination of the power of acceptance, irrevocable offers, acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and the battle of the forms, misunderstanding, and indefiniteness. Part II covers consideration, modification, and promissory estoppel. Part III covers the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every assigned case plus slide references.
- [Contracts I Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/contracts-i/contracts-i-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 266 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and tip in the Weeks 1–9 outline, across 16 topics from enforceable agreements and the objective theory through offers, termination, irrevocable offers, acceptance and silence, the battle of the forms, misunderstanding, indefiniteness, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the Statute of Frauds, duress, and misrepresentation, plus a set of integrated multi-issue problems. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

## Civil Procedure

Civil Procedure, Weeks 1–9 (Spencer, Civil Procedure: A Contemporary Approach, 7th ed., and the Federal Civil Rules Supplement). Covers the court systems and sources of procedural law, personal jurisdiction from Pennoyer through Ford, notice and service of process under Rule 4, federal question, diversity, supplemental and removal jurisdiction, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, the Erie doctrine through Shady Grove, pleading standards from Conley to Iqbal, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint under Rules 8, 12, and 55.

- [Civil Procedure Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/civil-procedure/civil-procedure-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–9 (Classes 1–16) on the Fall 2026 syllabus. Part I covers the civil justice system and the life of a lawsuit. Part II covers personal jurisdiction: the framework, the territorial era, minimum contacts, specific jurisdiction and the stream of commerce, and general, consent, and transient jurisdiction. Part III covers notice and service. Part IV covers subject-matter jurisdiction: federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal. Part V covers venue, transfer, forum-selection clauses, and forum non conveniens. Part VI covers the Erie doctrine. Part VII covers pleading, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every assigned case (29 main cases) plus slide references and supplemental readings.
- [Civil Procedure Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/civil-procedure/civil-procedure-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 255 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and tip in the Weeks 1–9 outline (Classes 1–16), across 15 topics: the court systems and sources of procedural law, the personal jurisdiction framework and territorial era, minimum contacts, specific jurisdiction and the stream of commerce, general, consent, and tag jurisdiction, notice and service under Rule 4, federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, removal, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, Swift to Erie, the modern Erie analysis, pleading and Rule 11, and responding to the complaint, plus a set of integrated multi-issue problems. Each question is an MBE-style fact pattern that asks what a court should do. The four choices are written to the same length and form, and the wrong ones are the usual bar traps: the right result for the wrong reason, a correct rule that does not apply, and a misstated rule. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

## Torts

Torts, Weeks 1–15 (Prosser, Wade & Schwartz, Torts: Cases and Materials, keyed to the 13th ed.). Covers liability based on fault, the intentional torts and their privileges, negligence (the reasonable person, professionals, negligence per se, proof, and res ipsa loquitur), cause in fact and proximate cause, duty and the failure to act, comparative fault, assumption of risk, limitations and immunities, premises liability, compensatory and punitive damages, joint and several liability, contribution, vicarious liability, strict liability, and nuisance.

- [Torts Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/torts/torts-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus, in syllabus order. The syllabus assigns the 15th edition of Prosser, Wade & Schwartz; the outline follows the 13th edition and maps each reading to its 13th-ed. chapter and cases. Part I covers the move from strict liability to fault. Parts II and III cover intent, battery, assault, false imprisonment, IIED, trespass to land and chattels, conversion, and the privileges: consent, self-defense, defense of others and of property, recapture, the shopkeeper's privilege, necessity, and discipline. Parts IV and V cover the negligence case, the Hand formula, the reasonable person, professionals and informed consent, negligence per se, notice, and res ipsa loquitur. Part VI covers but-for and substantial-factor causation, lost chance, alternative and market share liability, proximate cause, and superseding causes. Part VII covers duty and the failure to act. Part VIII covers comparative fault, assumption of risk, limitations, and immunities. Parts IX through XIV cover premises liability, damages, joint and several liability and contribution, vicarious liability, strict liability, and nuisance, and Part XV has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a case card for each principal case in the assigned pages. The Canvas-only readings are not briefed.
- [Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/torts/torts-restatement.txt): Document. The Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions sections the outline relies on, from Tentative Draft No. 3 (2024). Statutes of limitations and repose (§§ 1–16), aiding and abetting negligence, agreements to act negligently, the firefighter's rule, and liability for providing alcohol come with their black letter, Comments, and Illustrations. The Sections the ALI approved in 2022 come as black letter: apportionment (§§ 4 A–4 B and 27–37), immunities (§§ 1–10A), and loss of consortium (§§ 48 A–48 C). Search by word or section number, filter by outline topic, and open or close the Comments.
- [Torts Bar Exam Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/torts/torts-bar-exam-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 90 bar-style questions on all of Weeks 1–15, in three practice finals of 30, each sized like the final
